**Reformulation.** Two tuples agree in at most one coordinate exactly when their Hamming distance is at least 4. So C is a code of length 5, alphabet size 6, and minimum distance 4, and we want A₆(5,4).

**Upper bound.** The Singleton bound gives |C| ≤ 6^(5−4+1) = 36. Equality would require an orthogonal array OA(36,5,6,2). Such an array yields three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 6, and no such triple exists (N(6) = 1, so at most one pair of MOLS of order 6 exists). Hence |C| ≤ 35.

**Lower bound.** Taking the 25 codewords of the MDS code {(a + jb mod 5)_{j=0..4} : a, b ∈ F₅} gives 25 tuples over {0,…,4}. Adding (0,5,5,5,5) gives 26. Adding a second new word with a 5 in a different position would agree with it in 3 positions, so this simple extension stops at 26. Better constructions exist: two orthogonal partial Latin squares of order 6 can occupy 34 cells, which gives codes of length 4 and distance 3, but I could not construct a length-5 code above 26 by hand.

**Conclusion.** The exact value is the known table value A₆(5,4). I could not verify it, and my best recollection is 31, so treat that value as unconfirmed. What I can confirm is 26 ≤ |C|_max ≤ 35, with the 36 bound ruled out by the nonexistence of three MOLS of order 6.

ANSWER: 31
